Instrument.name: UNHT Nanoindenter
Instrument.description:
The nanoindenter is a highly sophisticated instrument designed to measure the mechanical properties of materials at the nanometer scale. It is a crucial tool in materials science, enabling researchers to explore the hardness, elastic modulus, and other mechanical properties of a wide array of materials with unprecedented precision through the nanoindentation process.
The nanoindentation process involves loading a precisely shaped indenter, often made of diamond, into the material surface with a controlled force. This force is then held constant for a specified period to allow for any time-dependent deformation, followed by unloading the indenter while recording the material's response. During this process, the nanoindenter continuously records the load and displacement, generating a load-displacement curve that provides insights into the material's mechanical behavior. Key measurements include indentation hardness (H), which measures the material's resistance to plastic deformation and is expressed in gigapascals (GPa); it is calculated by dividing the maximum applied load by the projected contact area at that load and Indentation Modulus (M), which measures the material's stiffness and is also expressed in GPa; it is derived from the initial unloading slope of the load-displacement curve, considering the deformations of both the sample and the indenter.
